title: Bash with DevOps tools
goal: Use jq on JSON APIs, wrap kubectl, docker, nginx and terraform in safe scripts (with mocks when the tool is not installed), and handle secrets without printing them.
setup: # P1: a GitHub-style releases API (served by a local test server)
# P2: what "kubectl get pods -o json" returns for the to-do app
# mock tools: they print or read files, they never touch a real cluster

printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' '# MOCK kubectl for practice' 'if [ "$1 $2" = "get pods" ] && [[ "$*" == *"-o json"* ]]; then cat ~/bash-practice/day26/pods.json; exit 0; fi' 'echo "[mock kubectl] kubectl $*"' > mockbin/kubectl
printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' '# MOCK docker for practice' 'if [ "$1" = images ]; then cat ~/bash-practice/day26/images.txt; exit 0; fi' 'echo "[mock docker] docker $*"' > mockbin/docker
printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' '# MOCK systemctl for practice' 'echo "[mock systemctl] systemctl $*"' > mockbin/systemctl

printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' '# MOCK nginx: "nginx -t -c FILE" checks that braces match and that lines end with ; { or }' 'FILE=$3' 'n=0; depth=0' 'while IFS= read -r line; do' '  n=$((n + 1)); l=${line%%#*}; l=${l//[[:space:]]/}' '  [ -z "$l" ] && continue' '  case $l in *"{") depth=$((depth + 1)) ;; *"}") depth=$((depth - 1)) ;; *";") ;; *) echo "nginx: [emerg] directive \"$(set -- $line; echo $1)\" is not terminated by \";\" in $FILE:$n" >&2; echo "nginx: configuration file $FILE test failed" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac' 'done < "$FILE"' 'if [ "$depth" -ne 0 ]; then echo "nginx: [emerg] unexpected end of file, expecting \"}\" in $FILE:$n" >&2; echo "nginx: configuration file $FILE test failed" >&2; exit 1; fi' 'echo "nginx: the configuration file $FILE syntax is ok" >&2' 'echo "nginx: configuration file $FILE test is successful" >&2' > mockbin/nginx

printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' '# MOCK terraform for practice' 'case "$1" in' '  fmt) [ -f .unformatted ] && { echo "main.tf"; exit 3; }; exit 0 ;;' '  validate) echo "Success! The configuration is valid."; exit 0 ;;' '  plan) echo "Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy."; [[ "$*" == *-detailed-exitcode* ]] && exit 2; exit 0 ;;' '  *) echo "[mock terraform] terraform $*" ;;' 'esac' > mockbin/terraform
# P3: an env file with secrets (fake values)
# P4: an nginx folder (practice copy) and a broken deploy script
printf '%s\n' 'server {' '    listen 80;' '    server_name todo.local;' '    location / {' '        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;' '    }' '}' > etc-nginx/sites-enabled/todo.conf
printf '%s\n' 'server {' '    listen 80;' '    server_name todo.local;' '    location /api/ {' '        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080' '    }' '}' > new-config/todo.conf
printf '%s\n' 'server {' '    listen 80;' '    server_name todo.local;' '    location /api/ {' '        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;' '    }' '}' > new-config/todo-good.conf

printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' '# Install a new nginx site config. Test it BEFORE reloading.' '# If the test fails: keep (or put back) the old config, do not reload, exit 1.' 'NEW=$1' 'cp "$NEW" etc-nginx/sites-enabled/todo.conf' 'systemctl reload nginx' 'nginx -t -c etc-nginx/sites-enabled/todo.conf' 'echo "deployed $NEW"' > deploy-nginx.sh
# P5: "docker images" output on the build server

printf '%s\n' 'todo-frontend 1.4.0 a1b2c3d4e5f6 2026-10-18' 'todo-frontend 1.3.2 b2c3d4e5f6a1 2026-10-02' 'todo-frontend 1.3.1 c3d4e5f6a1b2 2026-09-20' 'todo-backend 2.4.1 d4e5f6a1b2c3 2026-10-10' 'todo-backend 2.4.0 e5f6a1b2c3d4 2026-09-28' 'todo-backend 2.3.9 f6a1b2c3d4e5 2026-09-01' 'todo-backend 2.3.8 0a1b2c3d4e5f 2026-08-15' '<none> <none> 1b2c3d4e5f6a 2026-10-19' 'postgres 16 2c3d4e5f6a1b 2026-07-01' > images.txt

warmup.q: Which exit codes does a Nagios-style check use?
How do you send a JSON body with curl?
What does `set -x` print, and why can it be dangerous?
warmup.a: Each command with its values before it runs. It can print secrets (tokens, passwords) into CI logs.

warmup.q: What permission must an env file with passwords have?

problems.title: jq: read a JSON API
problems.situation: An install script must download the newest STABLE release of `todo-cli` from a GitHub-style releases API. The API returns JSON, so the user reads it with `jq` instead of grep. A local test server plays the API.
task: Start the test API: `python3 -m http.server 8131 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory api &`.
Get the JSON with `curl -fsS` and print the number of releases (`length`).
Print all tags with `-r` (raw text, no quotes).
Print only stable releases (`select(.prerelease == false)`) with their date.
Get the newest stable tag into a variable and build the download URL for the linux-amd64 asset.
hints: `jq '.[0]'` = first item; `.[]` = each item; `.tag_name` = a field.
solution: ASSET=$(curl -fsS "$API" | jq -r --arg t "$TAG" '.[] | select(.tag_name == $t) | .assets[] | select(.name | contains("linux-amd64")) | .name')

explanation.meaning: Number of items in the array.
Raw output: strings without quotes, ready for bash variables.
For each item, the field `tag_name`.
Keep only items where the condition is true.
String with fields inside (jq string interpolation).
Pass a bash value into jq safely as `$t`.
Filter the array, then take the first (newest) one.

problems.expected_output:
3
v2.5.0-rc1
v2.4.1
v2.4.0
=== stable releases ===
v2.4.1  2026-10-10
v2.4.0  2026-09-28
download: https://github.com/wicky/todo-cli/releases/download/v2.4.1/todo-cli-linux-amd64.tar.gz
mistakes: Parsing JSON with grep and cut: it breaks when the API changes spacing or field order. Use jq.
Forgetting `-r`: the variable contains quotes, like `"v2.4.1"`, and the URL is wrong.
Putting a bash variable inside the jq program in double quotes. Use `--arg` instead.
problems.interview_say: I read JSON from APIs with `curl -fsS URL | jq -r '...'`: `select` to filter, `.field` to pick values, `-r` for raw strings, and `--arg` to pass bash variables in safely.
problems.try_yourself: Print the total size of all assets of v2.4.1 in MB: `jq '[.[] | select(.tag_name == "v2.4.1") | .assets[].size] | add / 1048576'`.

problems.title: kubectl + jq: find unhealthy pods (mock)
problems.situation: The to-do app on Kubernetes is partly down. A script must list every pod with its phase, restarts and waiting reason, and suggest commands for the bad ones. kubectl is replaced by a mock that returns saved JSON, so no cluster is needed.
task: Put the mocks first in PATH: `export PATH="$PWD/mockbin:$PATH"`. Check `command -v kubectl`.
Print a table: name, phase, ready, restarts, waiting reason (`@tsv`, then `awk printf` for columns).
List pods that are not ready or have more than 5 restarts.
For each bad pod, print the next debug commands (`kubectl describe`, `kubectl logs --previous`).
solution: echo "$pod -> kubectl describe pod $pod | tail -n 20; kubectl logs $pod --previous"

explanation.meaning: Our fake `kubectl` runs instead of a real one (Day 5 PATH).
Save the first container status in a jq variable to keep the line short.
Alternative operator: use `-` when the value is missing (running pods have no waiting reason).
Tab-separated values, then aligned columns. (`column -t` does the same, if the package `bsdextrautils` is installed.)
The container starts and crashes again and again: check `kubectl logs --previous`.
The image cannot be pulled: wrong tag, or no access to the registry.

problems.expected_output:
kubectl here is: ~/bash-practice/day26/mockbin/kubectl
NAME                       PHASE    READY  RESTARTS  REASON
todo-frontend-7d9f8-abcde  Running  true   0         -
todo-backend-5c6b4-fghij   Running  false  7         CrashLoopBackOff
todo-backend-5c6b4-klmno   Running  true   1         -
todo-worker-6f7c9-pqrst    Pending  false  0         ImagePullBackOff
=== needs attention ===
todo-backend-5c6b4-fghij -> kubectl describe pod todo-backend-5c6b4-fghij | tail -n 20; kubectl logs todo-backend-5c6b4-fghij --previous
todo-worker-6f7c9-pqrst -> kubectl describe pod todo-worker-6f7c9-pqrst | tail -n 20; kubectl logs todo-worker-6f7c9-pqrst --previous
mistakes: Using `kubectl get pods | grep -v Running` to find problems: a pod can be `Running` but not ready, or restarting all the time.
Testing cluster scripts directly on production. Use `--dry-run=client`, a test namespace, or mocks like here.
problems.interview_say: For Kubernetes scripts I use `kubectl get -o json | jq` instead of parsing the table. A pod can be Running but not ready, so I check readiness, restarts and the waiting reason, then look at `describe` and `logs --previous`.
problems.try_yourself: Count pods per phase: `kubectl get pods -o json | jq -r '.items[].status.phase' | sort | uniq -c`.

problems.title: Secrets: env files, masking, and set -x leaks
problems.situation: A deploy script needs `DB_PASSWORD` and `API_TOKEN` from `.env`. In the last incident, the token appeared in the Jenkins log because of `set -x`. The user loads secrets safely, never prints them, and shows the leak and the fix.
task: Check `.env` permissions. If not 600, fix them before loading.
Load it with `set -a; source .env; set +a`. Print the DB host and a masked token (first 4 characters + `****`).
Show the leak: run a tiny `bash -x` command that uses the token. Then the safe version with `set +x` around the secret.
Make sure `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
hints: `set -a` exports every variable that is set while it is on.
solution: echo "=== the leak: set -x prints the value ==="
bash -xc 'curl_args="-H Authorization: token $API_TOKEN"; : "$curl_args"' 2>&1 | grep -c "$API_TOKEN" | sed 's/^/lines with the token in the trace: /'
echo "=== the fix: no trace around secrets ==="

bash -c 'set -x; echo deploy start; { set +x; } 2>/dev/null; curl_args="-H Authorization: token $API_TOKEN"; set -x; echo deploy done' 2>&1 | grep -c "$API_TOKEN" | sed 's/^/lines with the token in the trace: /'

explanation.meaning: Only the owner may read secrets (Day 3).
Load `KEY=value` lines and export them for child processes, then stop auto-export.
Show a short prefix only, to confirm which token is loaded.
The trace prints the expanded command, so the token is in the log.
Turn tracing off without printing the `set +x` line itself.
Never commit `.env`. Use CI secrets (Jenkins credentials, GitHub Actions secrets) or a secret manager.

problems.expected_output:
.env permission: 644
fixed to 600
DB host: db.todo.internal
API token: ghp_****  (length 23)
=== the leak: set -x prints the value ===
lines with the token in the trace: 2
=== the fix: no trace around secrets ===
lines with the token in the trace: 0
.env
mistakes: Passing a secret as a command argument (`mysql -pSecret`): other users can see it in `ps aux`. Use env variables or files.
`echo "token=$API_TOKEN"` in a debug line "just for now". It ends up in CI logs forever.
Storing secrets in the Docker image: anyone who pulls the image can read them.
problems.interview_say: I keep secrets out of code and logs: they come from CI secrets or a 600 env file, I never echo them, I mask them if I must show them, and I turn off `set -x` around commands that use them.
problems.try_yourself: Run `ps aux | grep -i token` while a command with a token argument runs (`sleep 30 --token=abc &` fails, try `bash -c 'sleep 30' token=abc &`). What can other users see?

problems.title: Find the bug: reload nginx only after a good test
problems.situation: `deploy-nginx.sh` installed a config with a missing `;` and reloaded nginx before testing it. In production, a bad reload can take the site down. nginx and systemctl are mocks here; the practice folder `etc-nginx` stands in for `/etc/nginx`.
task: Use the mocks: `export PATH="$PWD/mockbin:$PATH"`. Run `bash deploy-nginx.sh new-config/todo.conf; echo $?`.
Find 3 bugs: reload before the test, the test result is ignored, and no way back to the old config.
Fix it: back up the current config, copy the new one, `nginx -t`, reload only if OK, else restore and exit 1.
Test with the bad `new-config/todo.conf` and the good `new-config/todo-good.conf`.
hints: The real pattern is `nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx`.
Backup: `cp todo.conf todo.conf.bak` before copying the new file.
On failure: `mv todo.conf.bak todo.conf`, print an error, `exit 1`.
solution: cp etc-nginx/sites-enabled/todo.conf original.conf          # keep a copy for the second test
cp original.conf etc-nginx/sites-enabled/todo.conf          # undo the broken deploy
# Install a new nginx site config. Test it BEFORE reloading.
# If the test fails: keep (or put back) the old config, do not reload, exit 1.
echo "ERROR: $NEW failed the nginx test; old config restored, nginx NOT reloaded" >&2
cmp -s original.conf etc-nginx/sites-enabled/todo.conf && echo "the live config is still the old one"

explanation.meaning: Bug 1: nginx was reloaded with an untested config.
Bug 2: the script printed `deployed` and exited 0 after a failed test.
Bug 3: the old, working config was overwritten with no way back.
Test the configuration syntax. Real nginx: `sudo nginx -t` tests all of `/etc/nginx`.

explanation.part: if test; then reload; else restore
explanation.meaning: Validate, then apply, with a rollback path. The same idea as `terraform plan` before `apply`.
`mockbin/nginx` imitates nginx's messages; the real one is `sudo apt install nginx`.

problems.expected_output:
[mock systemctl] systemctl reload nginx
nginx: [emerg] directive "proxy_pass" is not terminated by ";" in etc-nginx/sites-enabled/todo.conf:5
nginx: configuration file etc-nginx/sites-enabled/todo.conf test failed
deployed new-config/todo.conf
exit code: 0
--- fixed, bad config ---
nginx: [emerg] directive "proxy_pass" is not terminated by ";" in etc-nginx/sites-enabled/todo.conf:5
nginx: configuration file etc-nginx/sites-enabled/todo.conf test failed
ERROR: new-config/todo.conf failed the nginx test; old config restored, nginx NOT reloaded
exit code: 1
the live config is still the old one
--- fixed, good config ---
nginx: the configuration file etc-nginx/sites-enabled/todo.conf syntax is ok
nginx: configuration file etc-nginx/sites-enabled/todo.conf test is successful
[mock systemctl] systemctl reload nginx
deployed new-config/todo-good.conf
exit code: 0
mistakes: `systemctl restart nginx` instead of `reload`: restart drops open connections; reload keeps serving with the old workers while new ones start.
Editing files directly in `/etc/nginx` on many servers by hand. Use config management (Ansible) or a container image.
problems.interview_say: Before reloading nginx I always run `nginx -t`. My deploy script backs up the old config, tests the new one, reloads only if the test passes, and restores the backup and fails otherwise.
problems.try_yourself: Add a health check after the reload (`curl -fsS localhost/health`). If it fails, restore the backup and reload again.

problems.title: Docker cleanup: keep the 2 newest tags (dry run)
problems.situation: The Jenkins build server's disk is full of old Docker images. Policy: for each repository keep the 2 newest tags, remove the rest, and remove dangling `<none>` images. The script prints `docker rmi` commands (dry run) so a human can check them first. `docker images` is a mock that prints saved output.
task: Use the mocks. Read `docker images` (here: repository, tag, id, created date).
Sort by repository, then by date (newest first).
With awk, count tags per repository and print the ones after the 2nd.
Also print dangling `<none>` images. Print every action as `docker rmi ...` (dry run).
hints: Real Docker: `docker images --format '{{.Repository}} {{.Tag}} {{.ID}} {{.CreatedAt}}'` gives the same columns.
solution: | awk -v keep="$KEEP" '$1 == "<none>" { print $3; next } ++seen[$1] > keep { print $1 ":" $2 }' \
echo "(dry run: nothing was removed. Real cleanup: pipe into 'sh' after checking, or use: docker image prune -f)"

explanation.meaning: Group by repository; newest date first inside each group.
Count rows per repository; print only after the 2nd.
Dangling images (no tag): remove by ID, then skip the counter.
Dry run: print, do not run (Day 4).
Built-in cleanup: `docker image prune -f` removes dangling images; `docker system df` shows usage.

problems.expected_output:
docker rmi 1b2c3d4e5f6a
docker rmi todo-backend:2.3.9
docker rmi todo-backend:2.3.8
docker rmi todo-frontend:1.3.1
(dry run: nothing was removed. Real cleanup: pipe into 'sh' after checking, or use: docker image prune -f)
mistakes: `docker rmi $(docker images -q)` removes everything, also images that running containers need (or fails with `conflict: unable to remove`).
Sorting dates as text works only for ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD). Other formats sort wrong.
problems.interview_say: To clean Docker images I list them with a fixed `--format`, group by repository, keep the newest N tags, remove dangling images, and print the commands first as a dry run. `docker system df` shows what uses the space.
problems.try_yourself: Change KEEP to 1. Which images are added to the list?

problems.title: terraform in CI: fmt, validate, plan exit codes (mock)
problems.situation: The infrastructure pipeline runs terraform in a shell step. `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` returns 0 (no changes), 1 (error) or 2 (changes). The script must not treat 2 as a failure. terraform is a mock here.
task: Use the mocks. Run `terraform fmt -check` and stop with a clear message if files are not formatted (create `.unformatted` to test).
Run `terraform validate`.
Run `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode -out=tfplan` and handle 0, 1 and 2 with `case`.
hints: With `set -e`, exit code 2 would stop the script. Capture it: `terraform plan ... || rc=$?`.
solution: terraform fmt -check > /dev/null || { echo "ERROR: run 'terraform fmt' first" >&2; exit 1; }
2) echo "changes found: saved to tfplan, waiting for approval" ;;

explanation.meaning: Fail when files are not formatted (exit 3).
Syntax and internal consistency, no cloud calls.
0 = no changes, 1 = error, 2 = changes present.
Catch the exit code so `set -e` does not stop the script on 2.
Save the plan; `terraform apply tfplan` later applies exactly what was reviewed.

problems.expected_output:
Success! The configuration is valid.
Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.
changes found: saved to tfplan, waiting for approval
exit code: 0
ERROR: run 'terraform fmt' first
exit code: 1
mistakes: Treating exit code 2 as a failure: the pipeline goes red whenever there are changes.
Running `terraform apply -auto-approve` without a reviewed plan in production.
problems.interview_say: In CI I run `terraform fmt -check`, `validate`, and `plan -detailed-exitcode -out=tfplan`. I handle exit code 2 as "changes found", not as an error, and apply only the saved plan after approval.
problems.try_yourself: Add `terraform show -no-color tfplan > plan.txt` (it will print a mock line here) and save it as a CI artifact.

problems.title: Script patterns for git, docker, kubectl and aws
problems.situation: The same few patterns appear in almost every DevOps script. The user runs them with a dry-run wrapper: a `run` function that prints the command when `DRY_RUN=1` and runs it otherwise.
task: Write `run() { if [ "${DRY_RUN:-0}" = 1 ]; then echo "+ $*"; else "$@"; fi; }`.
With `DRY_RUN=1`, use `run` for: docker build and push with a git-based tag, kubectl set image, rollout status, and an aws s3 cp.
Read the table of patterns.
hints: `"$@"` runs the command with its arguments exactly (Day 9).
A tag from git: `TAG=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo dev)`.
`kubectl rollout status deployment/X --timeout=120s` waits for the rollout.
solution: run() { if [ "${DRY_RUN:-0}" = 1 ]; then echo "+ $*"; else "$@"; fi; }
run kubectl set image deployment/todo-backend backend="$IMAGE" -n todo
run kubectl rollout status deployment/todo-backend -n todo --timeout=120s

explanation.meaning: One switch for the whole script: `DRY_RUN=1 ./deploy.sh` shows every command, changes nothing.
Commit id as image tag; `dev` when not in a git repo (like here).
Update the image, then wait until the new pods are ready (fails after the timeout).

problems.expected_output:
+ docker build -t registry.example.com/todo-backend:dev .
+ docker push registry.example.com/todo-backend:dev
+ kubectl set image deployment/todo-backend backend=registry.example.com/todo-backend:dev -n todo
+ kubectl rollout status deployment/todo-backend -n todo --timeout=120s
+ aws s3 cp build/report.html s3://todo-reports/dev/report.html
mistakes: `echo $*` style dry runs that lose quotes: the printed command looks fine, but the real one breaks on spaces. The real run uses `"$@"`.
problems.interview_say: My deploy scripts check that tools exist, use the git commit as the image tag, wait for `kubectl rollout status`, and support a `DRY_RUN` mode that prints every command instead of running it.
problems.try_yourself: Run the same lines with `DRY_RUN=0` and the mocks in PATH (`export PATH="$PWD/mockbin:$PATH"`). Which mock answers?

interview.q: How do you read a value from a JSON API response in bash?
interview.a: With jq: `curl -fsS URL | jq -r '.items[0].name'`. `-r` gives raw text; `select()` filters; `--arg` passes bash values in.

interview.q: How do you find Kubernetes pods that are not healthy?
interview.a: `kubectl get pods -o json | jq` and check phase, ready and restartCount; or `kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase!=Running`. Then `kubectl describe pod` and `kubectl logs --previous`.

interview.q: How do you handle secrets in shell scripts?
interview.a: Take them from CI secrets or a 600 env file, never hard-code or echo them, mask them in output, avoid `set -x` around them, and keep `.env` in `.gitignore`.

interview.q: How do you change an nginx config safely?
interview.a: Back up the old file, put the new one in place, run `nginx -t`, and reload only if the test passes; otherwise restore the backup.
0 = no changes, 1 = error, 2 = there are changes. CI scripts must not treat 2 as a failure.

recap.meaning: Raw values from a JSON array
Pass a bash value into jq
Load and export an env file

recap.example: sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
